objective: Make the new Codex-style open-web research lane the real scheduled job-search path across UK/Dubai/Japan/Singapore, alongside structured providers and Company Watch/watchlist, and prove it with live read-only acceptance. Retire the old scheduled behavior where the owner's Intern/Internship-only scanner is the sole discovery gate. Produce one unified nightly candidate manifest and morning Career Brief with source/funnel attribution.
prerequisites: agent-career-priority-company-watchlist-engine-2026-09-24 completed truthfully or has a valid empty-watchlist mode.
Existing unified discovery/high-recall tests remain green.
allowed_scope: Add a scheduled orchestrator that combines: current structured regional provider scan, open-web/Codex research, Company Watch findings, priority company watchlist findings, recruiter-watch exports when present and LinkedIn-export intake when present; then feeds one unified funnel.
The scheduled path must use the high-recall policy by default. Preserve intern_only only as an explicit diagnostic/compare mode, not the production discovery gate.

Run broad open-web searches for each configured region and role family. Explicitly test public LinkedIn Jobs discovery (for example indexed/public LinkedIn job URLs), Indeed/public results where accessible, Google/web-indexed vacancy discovery, and direct ATS/employer-careers discovery. Record each source class as reached, blocked, unavailable or not applicable based on real evidence.

Do not declare the live research lane production-ready unless at least one real current-web search mechanism is operational end-to-end. If Codex CLI cannot search the live web, use the implemented fallback provider interface and prove an allowed working source; otherwise stop with a precise blocker rather than falling back silently to fixtures.

For LinkedIn specifically, prove the system can discover at least a public LinkedIn Jobs result URL or truthfully record that public LinkedIn discovery is blocked in the environment. Do not use login/session cookies or local browser automation.
Validate discovered URLs where allowed, preserve current/live verification timestamps, and clearly separate validated-live, discovered-unverified and inaccessible results.

Replace/update the four ChiefCareerScan scheduled launchers so they call the unified scheduled orchestrator rather than regional_job_search.py alone; keep all scheduled runs read-only/dry-run with no automatic canonical tracker write or application action.
Keep per-region schedules staggered or otherwise concurrency-safe; enforce bounded run time, retry/idempotency, and source budgets so one blocked site cannot consume the whole scan.

Feed the resulting unified manifest/funnel metrics into Career Daily Brief: raw results, source coverage, semantic pass, eligibility pass, duplicates, tracker candidates, watchlist hits and explicit zero attribution.
Run an owner-safe live acceptance for each region with bounded queries and no external mutation, plus a whole-company regression. Canonical tracker hashes must be unchanged.
Document exact operational behavior, run commands, source coverage matrix, rollback to old scheduler, and no-go criteria.
stop_conditions: No autonomous tracker apply, job submission, outreach, LinkedIn mutation or account login.
No local interactive browser/GUI automation and no signed-in profile/cookie/session access.
Do not claim LinkedIn/Indeed/Google/source coverage from fixture tests alone.
Do not call a source 'empty' when it was inaccessible or blocked.
Do not cut over the schedule if live research has no functioning current-web mechanism.
notes: This is the operational cutover task missing from the first web-research contract. Current run_scheduled_scan.cmd still invokes regional_job_search.py and the old Career Ops lane title filter; this task makes the new research architecture the actual scheduled behavior.
